html:
Kuru was a kingdom of the Vedic period in northern India, around modern Delhi, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh. The map shows it around 500 BCE.

It formed around 1200 to 900 BCE, when the Kuru tribe united several clans of the Rigveda. Many scholars see it as the first real state in South Asia. Its kings and priests gathered the Vedic hymns into collections and set the rules for great public sacrifices, shaping Hindu ritual for good. Its people used Painted Grey Ware pottery and began to use iron. Its capitals included Asandivat and later Hastinapura.

The Mahabharata tells of a war between two branches of the Kuru family, the Pandavas and the Kauravas. By 500 BCE Kuru was only a minor state among the Mahajanapadas, and the centre of power had moved east to Magadha.
sum: Kuru was a kingdom of the Vedic period in northern India, around modern Delhi, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh. The map shows it around 500 BCE.
